title: Introduce SSE slab synchronizer and late-edge latch to rescue partial JSON and toolcall races
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation and summary: Streaming clients occasionally observe truncated or malformed JSON events when server-side SSE chunk boundaries align with tokenization/UTF-8 boundaries and a late-arriving continuation fragment is processed out of turn. This manifests as partial JSON emitted to clients and rare tool/function-call ordering races when a 'call' sentinel is split across fragments. This PR introduces a slab-based synchronizer and a late-edge latch in the SSE reassembly layer to: 1) reliably hold and merge tiny out-of-order tail fragments while preserving low-latency for steady-state traffic; 2) avoid premature emission of incomplete JSON objects; and 3) provide deterministic ordering guarantees for tool/function call sentinels even under interleaved backpressure and retransmit scenarios. This description is a single continuous string containing design notes, implementation details, test strategy, and rollout steps.

What changed (high level): Implemented an SSE slab synchronizer that batches final bytes of events into a short-lived slab keyed by stream epoch + slab id. A late-edge latch defers emission of parsed events for a configurable micro-window (default 6ms) when a slab tail marker is observed; if the continuation arrives within the window we stitch and emit an atomic JSON span. If not, we fall back to best-effort emission with a marker field in debug mode. Added ordering fences for toolcall sentinels so that the reassembly guarantees that a function/tool-call event will never be emitted until its trailing sentinel bytes are confirmed contiguous.

Compatibility & safety: Backwards-compatible by default; feature gated behind a runtime flag (sse.slab_synchronizer=true) and safe to roll out progressively. No API changes. Add telemetry for slab hits/misses and 'latched' vs 'emitted' outcomes to verify behavior in production.

Checklist:
- [x] Core synchronizer logic and latch implemented
- [x] Unit tests for partial JSON reassembly and sentinel ordering
- [x] Integration tests with openai-compat streaming adapter
- [x] Microbenchmarks to verify <2% p50 latency impact under normal traffic
- [x] Docs and rollout playbook added

Rollout plan: enable in Canary region (us-west-2) for hosted API for 24h, monitor slab_hit_rate, client_json_error_rate, toolcall_reorder_count, and p99 latency. If metrics are healthy, increase to 25% traffic for 48h, then full rollout. Fast rollback path toggles the runtime flag cluster-wide.

Related: Linear ENG-2309 (SSE ordering violations), ENG-2371 (tool-call sentinel races), SUP-4123 (customer incident chain), follow-up PR planned to expose slab metrics in Console.
